title: The experience of happiness: The role of internal contradictions in the system of personal values
abstract: Context and relevance. Happiness is one of the fundamental human experiences, yet its relationship with the internal consistency of personal values remains understudied. The theoretical framework of the study integrates D.V. Kashirsky's concept of personal values, L. Festinger's theory of cognitive dissonance, and the ideas of V. Frankl and A.N. Leontiev on the nature of happiness. Objective: to identify the relationship between the experience of happiness and internal contradictions in the system of personal values (the discrepancy between the importance of a value and its realization). Hypothesis. The experience of happiness is determined by the absence of pronounced internal contradictions in the system of personal values: the lower the level of dissonance between the importance of values and their realization, the higher the happiness index. Methods and materials. The sample consisted of 94 students from Moscow universities (86.2% female, age 17—39 years, M = 20.95; SD = 3.43). The following instruments were used: the KVS-2 personal values inventory (Kashirsky, 2014) and the Oxford Happiness Questionnaire (OHQ) adapted by A.M. Golubev and E.A. Dorosheva (2017). Pearson's correlation analysis and multiple regression analysis (Backward method) were applied. Results. Significant negative correlations between the happiness index and internal contradictions were found in 19 out of 25 life domains. The strongest associations were revealed for the domains of freedom (r = –0.426), harmonious life (r = –0.411), and stability (r = –0.400). The regression model identified contradictions in the domains of love (β = –0.209), freedom (β = –0.284), and stability (β = –0.212) as significant predictors of happiness, explaining 24.9% of its variance. Conclusions. The findings confirm that the experience of happiness is closely related to the internal consistency of personal values, particularly in the existentially significant domains of freedom, love, and stability. The results substantiate a two-level approach to psychological practice: harmonizing key value domains through concrete actions and fostering internal readiness for change.
